latent_mechanisms.clinical_meaning: Aggregate Reed-Sternberg cell mass and reactive cellular infiltrate across nodal and extranodal sites; drives mechanical, paraneoplastic, and metabolic downstream effects
Reed-Sternberg cell-derived IL-6, IL-1, TNF-α, IL-10 and chemokines (TARC/CCL17) producing fever (often Pel-Ebstein cyclical), drenching night sweats, weight loss, fatigue, and acute phase response

EBV LMP1/LMP2A-mediated NF-κB activation in Reed-Sternberg cells in the EBV-positive subset (~40–60% of classical HL, higher in mixed cellularity, elderly, immunosuppressed); conditions tumor biology and detectable circulating EBV DNA

Tumor-induced T-cell exhaustion (PD-1/PD-L1 axis), Th2 skewing, regulatory T-cell expansion, defective cell-mediated immunity, anergy; predisposes to herpes-zoster, PJP, fungal, and tuberculosis reactivation
Tumor-driven peripheral lymphadenopathy (cervical, supraclavicular, axillary, mediastinal), splenic infiltration, and hepatic lymphoid infiltration producing organomegaly and mass effect
Direct Reed-Sternberg cell and reactive lymphohistiocytic infiltrate in marrow (more common in advanced/stage IV disease) leading to cytopenias, especially anemia and thrombocytopenia
Cytokine-mediated and infiltrative hepatic involvement producing cholestatic enzyme elevation, hypoalbuminemia, and hepatomegaly; in severe HL can include vanishing bile duct syndrome
TNF-α/IL-6/IL-1 driven anorexia, lipolysis, sarcopenia, and ≥10% body weight loss qualifying as a B-symptom
IL-6-driven hepatic acute phase reactant production: CRP, fibrinogen, ferritin elevation, hypoalbuminemia, anemia of inflammation via hepcidin
Reed-Sternberg cell IL-5 secretion and Th2 microenvironment driving peripheral and tissue eosinophilia, contributing to pruritus and tumor microenvironment composition
Tumor-driven IFN-γ/IL-6/IL-18 milieu predisposing to lymphoma-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (LA-HLH/MAS), particularly with EBV-positive disease and immunosuppression

Release of intracellular potassium, phosphate, nucleic acids (→ uric acid) and LDH from rapidly lysing tumor cells; less common in HL than in high-grade NHL but possible with bulky disease and treatment initiation

Constellation of fever + lymphadenopathy + splenomegaly + hepatitis ± atypical lymphocytes that closely mimics infectious mononucleosis, miliary TB, brucellosis, HIV seroconversion, and other infectious FUO causes; clinically relevant for differential anchoring

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Reed-Sternberg cell mass scales cytokine output; bulky and advanced-stage disease more frequently produces clinical B symptoms
Tumor burden directly produces nodal, splenic, and hepatic enlargement

mechanism_edges.conditionality: predominantly in advanced (stage III–IV) or aggressive subtypes such as lymphocyte-depleted
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Hematogenous tumor spread into marrow occurs preferentially in advanced disease, defining stage IV
Tumor-mediated immune evasion (PD-L1 upregulation, Treg expansion) scales with disease burden

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV-positive classical HL subset
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: LMP1/LMP2A-mediated NF-κB activation drives Reed-Sternberg cell survival and proliferation in the EBV+ subset
Tumor-derived IL-6 directly drives hepatic acute phase response
TNF-α and IL-6 drive anorexia, lipolysis, and sarcopenia
Pyrogenic cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, TNF) raise hypothalamic set-point; classically Pel-Ebstein cyclical pattern (1–2 weeks fever, 1–2 weeks afebrile)
Drenching nocturnal diaphoresis is a classical B symptom driven by cytokine fever defervescence
Cytokine-mediated central fatigue syndrome
Unintentional weight loss >10% in 6 months defines B-symptom criterion
Combined IL-6 hepatic suppression and cachectic protein loss; albumin <4 g/dL is an IPS adverse prognostic factor
IL-6 directly induces hepatic CRP
Fibrinogen rise from acute phase response markedly elevates ESR (often >50 mm/hr; ESR is incorporated into early-stage HL prognostic stratification)
Ferritin is an acute phase reactant; further amplified if subclinical macrophage activation present
Hepatic IL-6 response increases fibrinogen synthesis
Hepcidin-mediated anemia of inflammation; hemoglobin <10.5 g/dL is an IPS adverse prognostic factor
Negative acute phase reactant suppression
LDH reflects proliferative tumor turnover; less specific in HL than in NHL but commonly elevated in advanced disease
Painless rubbery cervical/supraclavicular adenopathy is the hallmark presenting sign; alcohol-induced nodal pain is a classic but uncommon associated feature

mechanism_edges.conditionality: more common in advanced disease
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic involvement defines stage III; produces palpable splenomegaly
Hepatic infiltration in advanced disease
Cholestatic-pattern enzyme elevation from hepatic infiltration; can be paraneoplastic without overt infiltration

mechanism_edges.conditionality: advanced disease, vanishing bile duct syndrome rare but described
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Cholestasis from hepatic infiltration or paraneoplastic cholangiopathy
Marrow replacement adds to anemia of inflammation
Marrow involvement may suppress thrombopoiesis
Lymphopenia is an IPS adverse prognostic factor (<0.6 ×10^9/L or <8% of WBC) reflecting immune dysregulation and advanced disease

mechanism_edges.conditionality: leukocytosis with neutrophilia in some patients
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: WBC ≥15 ×10^9/L is an IPS adverse factor; reflects cytokine-driven myelopoiesis
Cellular immune defect (impaired delayed-type hypersensitivity) predisposes to herpes-zoster, PJP, fungal, mycobacterial reactivation
Translates immune defect into clinical infection events

mechanism_edges.conditionality: more pronounced in mixed-cellularity classical HL
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Reed-Sternberg IL-5 secretion drives peripheral eosinophilia
Eosinophil and Th2 cytokine-mediated paraneoplastic pruritus, sometimes severe and an early symptom

mechanism_edges.conditionality: EBV-positive subset
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Plasma EBV DNA is detectable and correlates with EBV+ HL tumor burden and prognosis
sIL-2R is shed from activated T cells in the tumor microenvironment; correlates with disease activity and elevated in HLH overlap
Tumor-derived IL-6 directly raises serum levels and correlates with B-symptom severity

mechanism_edges.conditionality: particularly EBV-positive HL, immunosuppressed patients, advanced disease
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Lymphoma-associated HLH is one of the most lethal complications of HL; presents with fever, very high ferritin, cytopenias, hypofibrinogenemia, hypertriglyceridemia
Macrophage activation produces extreme ferritin elevation (often >10,000 ng/mL)
TNF-α suppression of lipoprotein lipase produces hypertriglyceridemia (HLH-2004 criterion)

mechanism_edges.conditionality: with treatment initiation in bulky disease
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Nucleic acid catabolism elevates urate
Intracellular potassium release
Urate and phosphate crystal nephropathy

mechanism_edges.conditionality: bulky mediastinal mass, particularly nodular sclerosis subtype in young women
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Bulky anterior mediastinal mass can produce SVC syndrome and tracheal/bronchial compression
Untreated advanced disease has substantial mortality; modern combination therapy yields ≥80% 5-year survival in advanced disease and ≥90% in early stage
Lymphoma-associated HLH carries 30–60% mortality without rapid recognition and treatment
Opportunistic infections during chemotherapy-induced neutropenia/lymphopenia are major treatment-related mortality drivers
Fever + LAD + organomegaly + cytopenia presentation creates high prior on infectious FUO and produces diagnostic delay

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: mediastinal_lymphadenopathy_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: deep_abdominal_lymphadenopathy_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Classical Hodgkin lymphoma, especially nodular sclerosis, commonly presents with bulky mediastinal nodal packets.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Magnitude depends on anatomic subtype, stage, and whether disease is nodal-predominant or extranodal-predominant.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: metabolic_tumor_burden_activity is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: splenic_lesion_burden is an observable anatomic expression of lymphoma burden/distribution, not a separate diagnosis label.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when the lymphoma has measurable nodal or splenic mass burden on imaging or examination.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Nodal lymphoma burden can be observed as a measured nodal mass diameter; preserve reported cm instead of guessing 0..1 severity.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Only when the lymphoma has measurable nodal or splenic mass burden on imaging or examination.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic involvement or splenic lymphoma burden can be followed as raw splenic size when reported.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Lymphoma tumor burden commonly first appears as pathologic nodal disease; satellites describe where and how large.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Splenic lymphoma involvement is a parent imaging finding; size and burden are satellites/measurements.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Parent finding becomes present when the corresponding lymphoma distribution is clinically or radiographically present.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Extranodal lymphoma involvement is a parent finding; organ-specific extent is a satellite.
Lymphoma cytokine activity produces recurrent or persistent fever over weeks to months.
Fever and inflammatory markers persist when the driver is lymphoma biology rather than ordinary bacterial infection.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: Most prominent with pulmonary IVLBCL, mediastinal bulky disease, pleural/pericardial involvement, or severe anemia.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pulmonary, mediastinal, extranodal, or microvascular lymphoma involvement can produce breathlessness.

mechanism_edges.conditionality: More likely with airway/mediastinal compression or pulmonary infiltration.
mechanism_edges.clinical_rationale: Pulmonary or mediastinal lymphoma involvement can produce cough.
Pure lymphoma fever does not produce bacterial bloodstream growth, although secondary infection can override this.
Steroids or conventional anti-inflammatory treatment may transiently blunt symptoms but do not remove the Hodgkin tumor driver.
Hodgkin lymphoma can rarely mimic autoinflammatory disease through paraneoplastic inflammatory arthralgia or arthritis.
Cytokine-driven constitutional inflammation can produce myalgia.
Mediastinal nodal disease can cause pericardial involvement or lymphatic obstruction.

axes.shape_free_text: Often classical Pel-Ebstein cyclical pattern (1–2 weeks fever 38–40°C alternating with afebrile periods 1–2 weeks); can also be persistent low-grade or sustained high-grade fever; fever >38°C qualifies as a B symptom
axes.second_peak: cyclical recurrence every 1–2 weeks (Pel-Ebstein) characteristic but not invariably present

axes.shape_free_text: Drenching night sweats requiring bed/clothing change; B-symptom defining
Unintentional weight loss; >10% body weight in preceding 6 months qualifies as B symptom
Generalized pruritus, often severe and may precede diagnosis by weeks to months; sometimes considered a 'C' symptom
Progressive constitutional fatigue

Painless rubbery non-tender adenopathy, classically cervical/supraclavicular > axillary > mediastinal/inguinal; contiguous nodal spread; alcohol-induced nodal pain in <5% but pathognomonic when present
Palpable splenomegaly in advanced (stage III–IV) disease
Hepatomegaly in advanced disease
Often markedly elevated, frequently >50 mm/hr; ESR ≥50 (asymptomatic) or ≥30 (symptomatic) used in early-stage HL risk stratification
Elevated, often 20–150 mg/L; can be substantially higher in B-symptomatic disease
Elevated in proportion to tumor burden, generally less extreme than in high-grade NHL
Elevated due to acute phase response; very high (>10,000) suggests overlapping HLH
Often decreased; <4 g/dL is an IPS adverse prognostic factor
Anemia of inflammation common; <10.5 g/dL is an IPS adverse prognostic factor
Often modestly elevated with neutrophilia; ≥15 ×10^9/L is an IPS adverse factor
Lymphopenia in advanced disease; <0.6 ×10^9/L (or <8% of WBC) is an IPS adverse factor
Mild to moderate peripheral eosinophilia in a subset, particularly mixed-cellularity classical HL
Usually normal or reactive thrombocytosis; thrombocytopenia in marrow involvement or HLH overlap
Elevated with hepatic infiltration or paraneoplastic cholestasis; bone involvement raises bone fraction
Usually normal; cholestatic elevation in advanced hepatic involvement; rare vanishing bile duct syndrome can produce marked hyperbilirubinemia
Mildly elevated with hepatic involvement; modest values typical
Elevated and correlates with B-symptom severity
Elevated in HL, correlates with disease activity; marked elevation if overlapping HLH
Usually normal; markedly elevated if HLH supervenes
Usually elevated as acute phase reactant; decreased only if HLH/DIC supervenes
axes.second_peak: fall below 150 mg/dL if HLH/DIC develops

axes.shape_free_text: Mildly elevated baseline; spikes with treatment-induced tumor lysis
Detectable plasma EBV DNA in EBV+ classical HL; correlates with EBV+ tumor burden and prognosis; not specific to HL but supportive
Past-infection serology pattern reflecting EBV exposure history
Elevated due to cellular immune defect; further increased by chemotherapy and corticosteroids
Pre-test probability that fever-LAD-organomegaly syndrome reflects HL rather than infectious or autoimmune mimics; rises with biopsy results
Elevated with anti-CD20 (if used) and high-dose steroids; HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients require antiviral prophylaxis before chemotherapy
Cellular immune defect plus chemotherapy raises reactivation risk; routine screening (HBV, HCV, HIV, IGRA) before therapy
Affects regimen choice and timing; HL frequently affects young adults of reproductive age
Low at baseline; rises sharply if HLH triggers (EBV+ disease, immunosuppression, refractory disease) supervene
Increases with chemotherapy-induced neutropenia and steroid exposure; particularly herpes zoster, PJP, fungal, mycobacterial
Rises with tumor lysis at treatment initiation, especially in bulky disease
Bulky mediastinal disease can produce SVC syndrome and airway compromise, especially supine or under sedation
HL is associated with paraneoplastic hypercoagulability; central catheter–associated and SVC-syndrome–related thrombosis prominent

Aggregate disease-specific mortality hazard incorporating tumor burden, IPS prognostic factors, treatment response, and complication-driven excess mortality (HLH, treatment-related infection, organ failure). Modern combination therapy yields ~90% 5-year survival in early-stage and ~80% in advanced-stage disease
Imaging-visible mediastinal lymph node enlargement or nodal packets, not the CT test itself.
Imaging-visible retroperitoneal, mesenteric, porta hepatis, para-aortic, pelvic, or other deep abdominal nodal disease.
Large confluent nodal mass or bulky nodal conglomerate by exam or imaging.
Whole-body active lymphoma burden inferred from PET avidity, multi-station mass burden, or equivalent staging imaging.
Focal or multinodular splenic lymphoma lesion burden distinct from palpable splenomegaly alone.
Largest reported nodal or nodal-conglomerate diameter on CT/MRI/ultrasound or physical measurement; raw size, not a guessed severity score.
Largest splenic long-axis dimension on imaging; raw measurement when available.
Pathologic lymph node enlargement or nodal mass is present by examination or imaging. Parent finding for nodal distribution and size satellites.
Focal or multinodular splenic lesion suspicious for lymphoma is present. Parent finding for splenic lesion burden and splenic size satellites.
Extranodal mass, organ lesion, or tissue infiltration suspicious for lymphoma is present. Parent finding for organ-specific extranodal extent satellites.
History-level fever burden over days to months, distinct from a single measured body temperature.

axes.display_name: Lack of clinical response to standard antibacterial therapy
axes.shape_free_text: Persistent fever, inflammation, or organ findings despite antibacterial therapy that should have covered ordinary bacterial infection.
Patient-reported or observed breathlessness from pulmonary, cardiac, mediastinal, anemia, or systemic inflammatory involvement.
Dry or productive cough as a symptom axis; mechanism depends on pulmonary, airway, cardiac, or mediastinal involvement.
Probability that standard blood cultures grow a causative bacterium; expected to remain low in uncomplicated lymphoma fever.

axes.display_name: Persistent inflammatory syndrome despite anti-inflammatory/immunosuppressive treatment
axes.shape_free_text: Failure of fever, cytopenia/anemia, lymphadenopathy, or acute-phase reactants to resolve with glucocorticoid or conventional anti-inflammatory immunosuppression before a tissue diagnosis.
Paraneoplastic inflammatory arthralgia or arthritis can occur in Hodgkin lymphoma but is less central than in AOSD.
Constitutional cytokine-driven muscle pain can accompany Hodgkin lymphoma inflammatory presentations.
Small to moderate pericardial effusion from mediastinal lymphoma, lymphatic obstruction, or serosal inflammation.
Usually normal in untreated Hodgkin lymphoma; can rise with tumor lysis risk or fall with poor intake, renal handling, or treatment context.

Nonspecific infection-like inflammatory biomarker that may rise in aggressive lymphoma, cytokine-heavy presentations, organ dysfunction, or concurrent infection; lower expected range than bacterial sepsis.

axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Both downstream of IL-6/acute phase response; correlated but ESR rises and falls more slowly
Both acute phase reactants; partial decoupling possible if HLH drives extreme ferritin disproportionate to CRP
Both reflect chronic inflammatory state and disease severity; both are IPS adverse factors when low
Cyclical Pel-Ebstein temperature pattern emerges from intrinsic oscillation in cytokine drive
Both index reticuloendothelial expansion; advanced contiguous and hematogenous spread links them
Subclinical macrophage activation pressure raises probability of clinically declared HLH event

axis_couplings.conditionality: Large active lymphoma burden can raise turnover and inflammatory burden, but effect varies by subtype and bulk.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anatomic/metabolic lymphoma burden is a driver of LDH and inflammatory marker elevation rather than a laboratory test name.

axis_couplings.conditionality: Large active lymphoma burden can raise turnover and inflammatory burden, but effect varies by subtype and bulk.
axis_couplings.clinical_rationale: Anatomic/metabolic lymphoma burden is a driver of LDH and inflammatory marker elevation rather than a laboratory test name.

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Histologic confirmation by excisional lymph node biopsy required before initiating cytotoxic therapy
Bleomycin pulmonary toxicity risk amplified by pre-existing lung disease; PFTs (DLCO) before each cycle
Requires entecavir/tenofovir prophylaxis to prevent reactivation hepatitis

failure_modes: interim PET-positive after 2 cycles indicating chemoresistance
bleomycin pulmonary toxicity forcing regimen change

side_effects.interpretation: myelosuppression with neutropenic nadir 7–14 days post-cycle
neutropenic fever risk and herpes zoster reactivation
tumor lysis at first cycle in bulky disease

treatments.context_specific_role: Standard frontline curative regimen for classical Hodgkin lymphoma across stages; cycles every 4 weeks (days 1 and 15); guided by interim PET (Deauville score)

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Reserved for advanced-stage high-IPS disease with histologic confirmation
Higher infertility and secondary leukemia risk than ABVD; counseling and fertility preservation required

failure_modes: greater myelosuppression and treatment-related mortality than ABVD

side_effects.interpretation: high febrile neutropenia rate; G-CSF mandatory

treatments.context_specific_role: Intensified regimen for advanced-stage high-risk disease; higher tumor control but more toxicity than ABVD

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Targets CD30 universally expressed on Reed-Sternberg cells

treatments.context_specific_role: Used in A+AVD frontline regimen (replacing bleomycin) for advanced-stage HL; also for relapsed/refractory disease, post-autologous stem cell transplant consolidation, and as monotherapy

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Classical HL has 9p24.1 amplification with high tumor PD-L1 expression making it exquisitely PD-1 sensitive

failure_modes: immune-related adverse events (thyroiditis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, colitis, hypophysitis, type 1 diabetes)
treatments.context_specific_role: Relapsed/refractory classical HL; pembrolizumab is interchangeable; emerging in earlier lines

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Targets defined disease sites; consolidation after chemotherapy in early-stage and bulky disease

failure_modes: late effects: secondary breast/lung/thyroid cancer, coronary disease, hypothyroidism
treatments.context_specific_role: Combined-modality therapy for early-stage favorable/unfavorable disease and consolidation for bulky residual disease; minimized in modern era due to late toxicity

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Steroids amplify reactivation risk; screen and prophylax accordingly

side_effects.interpretation: typical steroid metabolic and neuropsychiatric effects

treatments.context_specific_role: Component of BEACOPP and many salvage regimens; rapid B-symptom relief and fever control; not used as monotherapy outside palliative or HLH-overlap settings

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Rasburicase preferred for high tumor burden / high TLS risk; allopurinol adequate for low–intermediate risk
Rasburicase causes severe hemolysis in G6PD deficiency; check before use

failure_modes: allopurinol does not lower existing urate, only blocks new production
treatments.context_specific_role: Tumor lysis prophylaxis with chemotherapy initiation in bulky HL; rasburicase if high risk

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Reduces duration and depth of chemotherapy-induced neutropenia; mandatory with BEACOPP, used after febrile neutropenia in ABVD

treatments.context_specific_role: Secondary prophylaxis after febrile neutropenia or primary prophylaxis with high-risk regimens

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Indicated when prolonged steroid exposure or profound CD4 lymphopenia expected

treatments.context_specific_role: PJP prophylaxis during heavy steroid- or BEACOPP-based therapy

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: Standard salvage for chemo-sensitive relapsed/refractory HL

side_effects.interpretation: severe transient pancytopenia and immune reconstitution period

treatments.context_specific_role: Salvage therapy in chemo-sensitive relapsed/refractory disease following second-line chemotherapy ± brentuximab

effect_modifiers.clinical_rationale: When lymphoma-associated HLH supervenes, etoposide-based therapy plus aggressive lymphoma-directed treatment is needed

treatments.context_specific_role: For HL-associated HLH; bridge to definitive lymphoma-directed therapy

history_of_symptomatic_IM.trajectory_modulation: EBV-positive HL more likely (mixed cellularity subtype), with detectable plasma EBV DNA

young_adult_15_to_35.trajectory_modulation: First peak; nodular sclerosis predominates, often with mediastinal bulk

older_adult_over_55.trajectory_modulation: Second peak; mixed cellularity and EBV-positive disease more frequent; worse prognosis

HIV_positive.trajectory_modulation: Strongly EBV-positive, often advanced stage with extranodal disease

chronic_immunosuppression.trajectory_modulation: Increased EBV-driven disease; modified treatment tolerability

rheumatoid_arthritis_sarcoidosis_SLE.trajectory_modulation: Modestly elevated risk possibly mediated by chronic immune activation and immunosuppressive therapy

supportive_care: histologic confirmation by excisional lymph node biopsy (core needle insufficient) before any cytotoxic therapy
staging FDG-PET/CT and contrast-enhanced CT; bone marrow biopsy now largely replaced by PET except in selected cases
baseline echocardiogram and pulmonary function testing (DLCO) before anthracycline and bleomycin exposure respectively
screening for HBV (HBsAg, anti-HBc), HCV, HIV, and latent tuberculosis (IGRA) before chemotherapy with antiviral or anti-tuberculous prophylaxis as indicated
fertility counseling and preservation (sperm banking, oocyte/ovarian tissue cryopreservation) before gonadotoxic regimens, particularly BEACOPP
pneumococcal, influenza, and SARS-CoV-2 vaccination before therapy when feasible; avoid live vaccines during and after immunosuppression
tumor lysis syndrome risk stratification with hydration and allopurinol or rasburicase prophylaxis at chemotherapy initiation in bulky disease
PJP prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) and herpes zoster prophylaxis (acyclovir/valacyclovir) during prolonged corticosteroid or intensive chemotherapy
G-CSF support per regimen risk and after febrile neutropenia
interim PET (after 2 cycles, Deauville score) to guide response-adapted therapy
cardiopulmonary monitoring during bleomycin therapy with prompt drug discontinuation if pulmonary toxicity (cough, dyspnea, DLCO decline)
anterior mediastinal mass airway and SVC syndrome assessment before sedation or general anesthesia
psychological support and survivorship planning given young patient demographic
long-term surveillance for late effects: secondary malignancy (breast, lung, thyroid, AML/MDS), cardiovascular disease, hypothyroidism, infertility, pulmonary fibrosis

rapid recognition and treatment of lymphoma-associated HLH (extreme ferritin, cytopenias, hypofibrinogenemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hepatosplenomegaly) with HLH-directed therapy plus lymphoma-directed therapy
venous thromboembolism prophylaxis consideration in hospitalized patients and those with bulky mediastinal/SVC syndrome
